name: Taurine

lead: Taurine is a sulfur-containing amino sulfonic acid found in high concentrations in muscle, heart, retina and brain. It is common in energy drinks and available as a standalone supplement.

In recovery and longevity discussions it is promoted for exercise performance, cell protection and general health. Reviews show small effects on some metabolic and performance outcomes, and evidence for appearance-related benefits is thin.

paras: Taurine contributes to osmoregulation, bile-salt conjugation, calcium handling and antioxidant defense, and may modulate inhibitory GABA and glycine receptors. How oral supplementation translates to measurable benefits in healthy adults is not well established.

Considered safe at typical intakes, with rare mild gastrointestinal effects. Most concerns about energy drinks relate to caffeine rather than taurine. It is legal and sold as a supplement and food additive.
